dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Ugh, how worrisome... What should I do next?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's got you so worried?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: As a civil officer of the Shogunate, what else could I be worried about?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: I've already requested the Tri-Commission to handle the matter. Although I am the head of the civil office, I don't have any actual power. All I can do is worry all day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Tri-Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: As an outsider, what do you think of each of the Commissions?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: ...Forget it, what's the point in asking you such a question? But in light of the situation, let me speak with you frankly.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: The Kanjou Commission strictly enforces the Sakoku Decree, even Ritou is sealed off from the outside world. But I'm afraid this policy is only making matters worse for Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission aggressively uses their military might. When faced with the issue of the Sangonomiya rebels, they decided to suppress it solely with brute force. They ignore the hearts of the people, and someday will pay the price for that.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: As for the Yashiro Commission... They do indeed empathize with the people in their handling of ceremonial affairs, but without any military or financial power they are relatively weak.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Distributing aid during wartime can provide temporary relief to address the problem, but it is no long-term solution. It is gradually consuming the strength of the Kamisato Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Ugh... Just talking about it makes me more worried.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take care of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Okay, you too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you fretting about?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: As a civil officer of the Shogunate, what else could I be worried about?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Inazuma's gone through so many changes recently. I can only hope that the Tri-Commission is up to the challenge.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Tri-Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Hmm, actually, as an outsider, what do you think of the way the Tri-Commission is running at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: ...You know what, never mind. I don't think even they know what's going on themselves, let alone you.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: The Kanjou Commission's been buried in mountains of old accounts that need settling ever since their dealings with the outlanders were exposed. I've got no clue whether they'll make it out of this one or not.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission doesn't bear mentioning. The Kujou Clan's situation is very worrying. Who knows what Her Excellency's final judgment will be...

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: The Yashiro Commission on the other hand seems to have come out of these twists and turns even better than before, the whole business with one of their retainers defecting during the Vision Hunt Decree notwithstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Whatever the case, I just hope they can fix this mess. I doubt Her Excellency will have much mercy otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take care of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Okay, you too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Been busy with anything lately?

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Lately, you say... Well, I have been thinking about land management of late.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: I'm not sure if you've noticed, but there is an island to our south known as Tsurumi Island that has been locked off by perpetual fog, the point where few people dare enter.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: For some unknown reason, the fog has cleared recently, so I and my colleagues are presently discussing if we should put a team together to survey the area.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: If we could undertake some development there, it would be quite the contribution to Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: However, the situation isn't all that clear yet, so it may be some time yet before we come to a conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Almighty Shogun...

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Inazuma has undergone so many changes in such a short time. In my experience, Her Excellency will not just stand idly by.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: I know I fret a lot, but as an officer of the Shogunate, I have utmost faith in Her Excellency's might.

dialogues.speaker: Nagaoka Hidemitsu
dialogues.text: Inazuma will move into a new era under her guidance for sure.
